strengths: The paper addresses an important question: how adversarially trained networks can generalize on clean inputs while retaining a large robust generalization gap.

The proposed mechanism—learning shared signal while memorizing sample-specific noise—is interpretable. Combining representation complexity with explicit feature-learning dynamics is a useful conceptual approach.

Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10, and synthetic data provide qualitative illustrations of the phenomenon. Tracking signal and noise components makes the proposed mechanism amenable to empirical investigation.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated assumptions. Consider a uniform distribution on inputs ±e1 with corresponding labels ±1, radius δ=1/4, and f_clean(x)=x1+8 ReLU(x2). This satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3. With N growing, both atoms occur with nonvanishing empirical frequency with high probability, so vanishing robust training error forces zero robust population error. No CGRO classifier can then exist. The argument needs additional assumptions controlling how much of the population the training neighborhoods cover.

The representation construction has further substantive gaps. Assumption 4.2 separates opposite classes, but does not imply that all training balls are disjoint; consequently, the proposed algebraic rewriting of f_S fails when same-class balls overlap. Moreover, Appendix F claims uniformly vanishing approximation error for a generally discontinuous f_S using continuous ReLU networks. Softening indicators does not establish this claim, and transferring approximation error to classification guarantees requires additional margin and boundary control.

Theorem 5.9 does not establish the stated robust training guarantee. Definition 5.6 optimizes over perturbations restricted to the true signal direction, leaving noise patches unchanged. Definition 3.3 measures robustness over the entire norm ball. Appendix E.12 infers vanishing robust training error directly from the restricted adversarial loss, which only controls the smaller attack set. This mismatch undermines the central claim that the dynamics produce a CGRO classifier under the original definition.

The clean-generalization proof in Appendix E.12 uses an invalid concentration argument: a cubic polynomial of Gaussian noise is generally not sub-Gaussian. Projections through different neurons also share the same noise and are correlated. The asserted weight-norm bounds do not follow merely from the aggregate memorization statistic. A valid Gaussian-polynomial concentration argument and quantitative control of the learned weights are needed.

The supplementary global-flatness bound in Theorem B.1 is also incorrect as stated. A constant, nonzero-logit classifier has zero input gradient everywhere, but its population logistic loss can exceed empirical loss with constant probability because sampled label frequencies fluctuate. The displayed bound would forbid this gap. Appendix G additionally retains density-estimation error terms that are not accounted for in the claimed final rate.

The experiments do not adequately validate the theoretical conclusions. The synthetic setting uses δ=α=10, violating the strict δ<α condition and allowing complete removal of the only informative patch; poor robust test performance therefore has an explanation independent of the proposed learning dynamics. Model-size sweeps and local-flatness measurements provide qualitative correlations, but do not establish exponential capacity requirements or uniquely identify robust memorization. PGD attack settings, optimizer schedules, repeated-run variability, and synthetic evaluation sample sizes are insufficiently specified for reliable reproduction and assessment.

The advance over prior work needs sharper justification. The paper describes Li et al. (2022) as already establishing an exponential robust-representation lower bound for linearly separable distributions. Such distributions also admit polynomial-size clean classifiers, so broadening the allowed distribution class does not by itself strengthen an existential lower bound. Furthermore, the static CGRO definition does not establish the late-training deterioration commonly associated with robust overfitting. These scope concerns matter, but the decisive reason for rejection is that several central mathematical guarantees are unsupported or false as stated.
